intro: Ordinary cross-entropy can receive many small contributions from easy examples. Focal loss weights each contribution by how uncertain the correct-class prediction is.
task: Compute a stable multiclass focal loss from logits and integer class labels. Compare gamma zero with positive gamma to isolate the focusing effect.
requirements: logits is a nonempty (N,C) real array and targets is an integer array of shape (N,) with labels in [0,C); booleans are not labels.
For each example, obtain the correct-class log probability using log-softmax. Return the batch mean of -alpha*(1-p_target)**gamma*log(p_target).
alpha is a nonnegative finite scalar and gamma is a nonnegative finite scalar. This scalar alpha weights every example equally; it is not a per-class balancing vector.
Do not add epsilon to the target probability. Compute its log directly from shifted logits so a wrong confident prediction can have a large finite loss.
Inputs must be real numeric values with finite magnitude at most 1e30. Leave inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Stay in log space
hints.body: Subtract the row maximum, then subtract log(sum(exp(shifted_logits))) to obtain log probabilities without taking log of an underflowed zero.

hints.title: Recover just the needed probability
hints.body: Gather the target log probabilities first. Their exponentials provide p_target for the focusing factor.

explanation: At gamma zero, the focusing factor is one and the loss is scalar-alpha-weighted cross-entropy. Larger gamma downweights easy examples more strongly, without proving better model performance.
The upstream implementation adds 1e-8 before taking the logarithm. This adaptation uses log-softmax instead, avoiding the artificial loss cap on extreme wrong predictions.
This exercise ports the upstream forward objective to NumPy. It adds explicit validation, deterministic edge cases and the gamma-zero limit; it does not provide automatic gradients.
